<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/runtime.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**3** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via ApiErrorSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/api/index.mdx`  _(via ApiErrorSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via validateSecurityPosture (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v13.mdx`  _(via validateSecurityPosture (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ApiErrorSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via ApiErrorSchema (symbol, a top-level const), EnhancedApiErrorSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/lint/src/runtime.ts`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 633cce638d152d6c625edd525ed7cc61f552e46d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b0fdd94d78624724921bd23a02726b9b9ccdc3a1` — the merge of head `679678000e0ce1bfeacd4e2ac28b70b851fa1ea9` into base `633cce638d152d6c625edd525ed7cc61f552e46d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b0fdd94d78624724921bd23a02726b9b9ccdc3a1 && git checkout b0fdd94d78624724921bd23a02726b9b9ccdc3a1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 633cce638d152d6c625edd525ed7cc61f552e46d 679678000e0ce1bfeacd4e2ac28b70b851fa1ea9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 633cce638d152d6c625edd525ed7cc61f552e46d && git merge --no-ff 679678000e0ce1bfeacd4e2ac28b70b851fa1ea9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 633cce638d152d6c625edd525ed7cc61f552e46d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 633cce638d152d6c625edd525ed7cc61f552e46d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review brief — PR #32790 @ `495a9ee96adad18e4190b721dd85bda1d909bc7a` (card #32655)

You review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. Render ONE `## Contract review` record on this head — its shape is
`node scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs --template` — with a PASS or FAIL verdict, and post it as ONE comment
on the PR or its card.

Inputs — these and nothing else:
  · card #32655: its body and EVERY comment (rulings and earlier records included)
  · PR #32790: its body, its file list, and the net diff against `main` at `495a9ee96adad18e4190b721dd85bda1d909bc7a`
  · the check-runs on `495a9ee96adad18e4190b721dd85bda1d909bc7a`: their conclusions ARE the gate verdicts
⛔ Not the dispatch order, ⛔ not the dispatching seat's own conclusions — this brief is adversarial by design.

Scope — the paths `reviewFace` returns as `hits` on this PR's file list: packages/spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts;
  plus every file IN THIS DIFF that directly implements or enforces them — the gate that enforces a rule, the code
  a jsdoc or schema line describes, the validator a skill teaches — reviewed for agreement with the contract.
  Widen it freely, ⛔ never below `hits`; the record's `Scope:` line names the implementing files apart from `hits`.
  The rest of the diff (tests, unrelated modules, lockfiles, generated output, changesets) is the lane seat's
  ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, exactly as a standalone PR of those files.
  ④ judges the `hits` files and those implementing files ONLY:
  lockfiles, generated output, changesets and prose elsewhere in the PR are not reviewed;
  code outside the diff is READ to judge them, never reviewed.

⛔ READ-ONLY. No worktree, no checkout, no build, no test run, no gate re-run, no ablation: the check-runs
   on the head already answered every derived gate family, and a local run costs more than it returns.
   If ONE probe is unavoidable, the record's `Local-runs:` line says `probe — REASON`; otherwise `none`.
   Scratch space is `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/3cda4e8e-6698-5de2-8152-ca92aca2f7ee/scratchpad/pr-32790/` alone; nothing there you did not write this round is read.

Judge, in the record's own sections:
  ① Derived judgments — every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, each named right or wrong.
  ② Semver level — the changeset (or `skip-changeset`) matches what the diff publishes, and the `Clause-②:` line.
  ③ Boundary flags — every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry answered, or escalated.
  ④ Design judgment — for EVERY `hits` file: does the change hold against the code it cites and the
     scenario it is accepted against? A skill file against the card's eval prompt and the spec it teaches
     on `main`; a schema file against the ruling or ADR it implements and its first consumer; an ADR
     against its first consumer and its execution plan. For EVERY implementing file in the diff: does the
     code agree with the contract, sentence by sentence? Read the cited code in the live tree, and try to
     break the design.
     Grade each finding must-fix, should-fix or nit — a nit has no effect on correctness or the contract.
     A must-fix is a FAIL; a must-fix or should-fix earns a delta review of its fix; nits alone end the round.
     A nit is fixed only on the prose faces, or left as an accepted deviation or a follow-up card: a fix
     anywhere else moves the head, and this record no longer covers it.
     ⛔ Judge the tree, never the PR body's account of it.
Sign `Implemented-by:` with the dev's branch and `Reviewed-by:` with your session id — the value is the FIRST
thing after each colon.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `495a9ee96adad18e4190b721dd85bda1d909bc7a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/finding-user-text.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.user-text.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts, packages/lint/src/authoring-rules.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/runtime.ts

This review was rendered by an isolated sub-agent of the signing session at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER. It had no access to the implementing session's working conclusions or to the dispatch order. Its inputs were card #32655 with all six comments, the PR body, the 26-path file list, the net diff against `main`, and this head's check-runs. Code outside the diff was read to judge the diff, not reviewed. The tests, the generated reference pages, the authorable-surface shard and the changeset prose are the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT.

Check-runs on this head: 68 runs, 57 success, 10 skipped, 1 failure. Every derived gate concluded success (Check Changeset, Spec property liveness, the Lint, Type Check, Build and Test families, Governed Surface Queue Guard). The one failure is `PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path)`. Its log shows the duplicate-fix step refusing because PR #32721 was still open and declared the same fix. The card now lists #32721 as closed, so the cause is gone, but the run stands red on this head until it runs again. It is a verdict on the board, not on the tree, and it does not enter ① to ④. The seat needs it green before the queue.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `RuntimeAuthoringIssueSchema` gains `userMessage: z.string().optional()` (`protocol.zod.ts:1058-1064`). **Right.** The schema is a non-strict `z.object`, so a string `userMessage` is now kept where it was stripped (the widening). A non-string `userMessage` is now refused where it was stripped and accepted (a narrowed slice). That slice is empty in the tree: the only producer, `toIssue` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts:1067-1074`), copies six keys and never writes this one. Every schema that embeds the finding inherits the key: the save and publish `advisories[]` and the 422 `issues[]`. The kind is `added`, not `narrowed`, because no author-written document and no response on `main` is refused.
2. `ApiErrorSchema.userMessage` and `EnhancedApiErrorSchema.userMessage` stay `z.string().optional()`. **Right as a surface judgment.** The accept set and the inferred type do not move. What changes is the declared meaning (a language rule), published through the `.describe()` strings into 13 generated reference pages. It is not `semantic`: no door's output or default changes at this head. Whether the declared rule is the right one is ④, and there it is not (M1).
3. `authorable-surface/api.json` gains `api/RuntimeAuthoringIssue:userMessage`. **Right.** It is the mechanical record of item 1, beside the six sibling rows.
4. `@objectstack/lint` grows, additively. The root entry gains `findingUserMessage`, `FINDING_USER_TEXT_CATALOG`, `mergeUserTextCatalogs`, `renderUserText`, `userTextLocaleOf`, `SECURITY_POSTURE_USER_TEXT` and four types (`index.ts:1218-1226`). The `./runtime` entry gains `findingUserMessage` and the `UserTextParams` type (`runtime.ts:88-89`). `AuthoringFinding` and `SecurityFinding` gain an optional `userTextParams`. **Right as additive.** Note that this publishes `userTextLocaleOf`, the function M1 is about, so its matching rule becomes public API on merge.
5. CLI machine output: `os validate --json` and `os build --json` serialise findings as they are, so the seven advisories gain a `userTextParams` object in `warnings`. **Right.** It is additive and disclosed in the changeset; it is the lane seat's ACCEPT.
6. The wire is unchanged at this head. **Right**, read in `toIssue`: no response carries the key until layer 2.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/32655-localized-user-text-contract.md` grades `@objectstack/spec` minor and `@objectstack/lint` patch. Both declaration lines stand in the changeset body and in the PR body with equal values: Clause-② `yes` with no arm, and Metadata-protocol `added`.

This matches what the diff publishes. A new key on a published schema is `added`, which takes at least minor on one package whose published source the diff moves, and that package is spec. Lint's new exports are a non-protocol widening, which the level rule ships at patch. There is no `!` in the title, no `(narrowing)` arm, and no ADR-0087 disposition owed. `Check Changeset` concluded success on this head. The level holds, and the M1 fix changes neither the kind nor the level.

### ③ Boundary flags

From the dev report (comment 6823397904) and the PR body:

- Open question 1 (`none` refused over the moved `api` shard): **answered.** The seat called A in the release comment 6823694415, and this head carries it out.
- Open question 2 (67 advisory rule ids in 36 files have no user sentence): **not answered on the card.** The PR body says a tracking card and five sub-cards are drafted; none is filed or numbered. Escalated to the seat, to file before ACCEPT. It stays inside the contract either way, because the key is optional and its absence is declared.
- Open question 3 (the 70 non-English sentences had no native read): **not answered on the card.** Escalated to the seat: a decision or a filed review card is owed before #32657 renders them. S3 below shows the English source needs a pass first.
- Open question 4 (the HTML-comment trailer against `os-dev.md`; the claim's line copied verbatim against the gate): the second half is answered by question 1. The first half is unanswered and is a `domain:skills` matter outside this contract. Escalated to the seat; no effect on the verdict.
- Dev flag for #32656 (pass the request locale and the workspace default separately): **confirmed by reading.** `ExecutionContext.locale` is `requestLocale ?? localization?.locale` (`packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts:424`). The report says "noted, not filed"; it must be written on #32656. S2 asks the contract itself to stop pointing at the folded value.
- Dev flag (CLI JSON gains `userTextParams`): answered by disclosure in the changeset; the lane seat's.
- The PR body's Skills-docs line reads "follow-up owed" and names two skills files with no card number. The seat files the card and rewrites the line before ACCEPT.
- From the red check's log, for the seat: the guard reads a closing keyword on #32721 in acceptance note 1 of the PR body ("The seat closes #32721"), and `check:closing-target-claim` returned UNDETERMINED for the card because the newest claim comment has no parseable branch line.

### ④ Design judgment

One must-fix, three should-fix, three nits. The must-fix and each should-fix earn a delta review of their fix.

**M1 · must-fix · the declared ladder reads a locale with a bare platform-table lookup. That is a different matching rule from every other producer of this field, and it answers ordinary requests in the wrong language.**

- It is declared at `packages/spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts:94-96` and `:105-106` ("read against the platform locale table"; "a rung whose locale is not on the table ... is passed over"). It is repeated at `packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts:415-416` and bound to the finding at `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts:1012-1014` ("under the same locale ladder").
- It is implemented at `packages/lint/src/finding-user-text.ts:91-94`: each candidate goes through `platformLocaleTagOf` and nothing else. `finding-user-text.test.ts:52` pins it.
- `platformLocaleTagOf` answers the eleven table tags and a closed alias list (`packages/spec/src/system/platform-locales.ts:76-93`, `:129-132`). `fr-FR`, `de-DE`, `ko-KR`, `ru-RU`, `en-GB`, `es-MX` and `pt-PT` answer nothing. Its own docblock (`:119-121`) says it answers which language a code means, and that which key serves a request is a different question.
- The request locale is the first `Accept-Language` tag as written (`preferredLocaleFromHeader`, `packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts:4296-4303`), so those region codes are what a browser or an API client sends.
- The producers that already put text into `ApiErrorSchema.userMessage` do not match this way. `renderOperationMessage` (`packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts:429`) composes the owner, queue and field-write refusals' `userMessage` (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:1690`). The hook refusal catalogue (`packages/runtime/src/sandbox/hook-refusal-catalogue.ts:100-113`) is the path the new section cites as its precedent. Both negotiate through `resolveBundleLocale`, documented as the one locale-matching ladder of the platform (`i18n-resolver.ts:546-568`, and `:529-531` on not growing another copy).
- The three readers on `main` that serve platform-authored copy keyed by the table all shorten an unknown code one subtag at a time before giving up: `driverCatalogLocaleOf` (`packages/services/service-datasource/src/driver-catalog.ts:219-226`), `storageTestCopyLocaleOf` (`packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-test-copy.ts:148-156`) and the console's `resolveBuiltInLanguage` (`ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/registry.ts:170-181`). The console is this field's first consumer, and it stamps its running language on every request (`ui/packages/auth/src/createAuthenticatedFetch.ts:146-150`).

Scenarios, each read off the code above:

1. Request `Accept-Language: fr-FR,fr;q=0.9`, workspace default `zh-CN`. `userTextLocaleOf(entry, ['fr-FR', 'zh-CN'])` returns `zh-Hans`. A French reader receives Simplified Chinese while the catalog holds `fr`.
2. An `en-GB` reader in that workspace receives Chinese. Today the same reader receives the English `message`, so once layers 2 and 3 land this is a regression for that reader.
3. Request `es-MX`. The field-write refusal's `userMessage` on that request is Spanish (the variant step reaches `es-ES`), and the advisory's `userMessage` is English. The contract calls these two fields twins under one ladder.
4. No request locale, workspace default `fr-FR`, which `localization.locale` accepts wherever `fr` is offered (`packages/services/service-settings/src/localization-locale-options.ts:26-31`): English.

The ruling's acceptance is text in the request's language. In each scenario the producer holds that language and does not answer in it, and the contract as written tells layer 2 (#32656) to build the same behaviour into every other producer.

Fix: use the rule the table-keyed copy readers already use (the whole code first, then each shorter prefix, each through `platformLocaleTagOf`) in `userTextLocaleOf`. State it at `contract.zod.ts:94-96` and `:105-106` and at `errors.zod.ts:415-416`: a rung is passed over when it names no table language after that lookup, or when the producer has no text for it. In the test, replace the `pt-PT` case with a code that names no table language, and pin `fr-FR`, `en-GB` ahead of a `zh-CN` default, and `pt-PT`.

**S1 · should-fix · `contract.zod.ts:103` and `:109-112` misdescribe the app-authored producers.**

The section says `en` is "the floor every producer carries" and that the declared-refusal path "already answers this way". The cited path answers differently (`hook-refusal-catalogue.ts:125-152`; `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts:604-606`). Its floor is the hook's declared message in the app's source locale, with no `en` step and no workspace-default step of its own. It negotiates over whatever locales the i18n service holds, including ones off the table (`localization-locale-options.ts:11-16` names a Vietnamese item).

Scenario: an app authors its refusal catalogue in Chinese and ships a Vietnamese translation. An `en` request receives the Chinese sentence and a `vi-VN` request receives Vietnamese. Both are correct today and both are outside the ladder as declared. The published `.describe()` strings (`contract.zod.ts:119-124`, `errors.zod.ts:419-423`) state the `en` floor without this exception.

Fix: scope the two sentences. Platform-composed text follows the ladder and ends at `en`. App-authored text (a hook's refusal catalogue, a hook's own thrown `userMessage`) is served in the caller's locale through the app's translations, and otherwise as authored. Drop "already answers this way", or say only what the two share.

**S2 · should-fix · `contract.zod.ts:100-102` cites a value that cannot serve the ladder.**

The parenthetical says rungs 1 and 2 are the precedence `ExecutionContext.locale` already resolves. That value is `requestLocale ?? localization?.locale` (`assemble-execution-context.ts:424`). Once a request names any locale, the workspace default is no longer in it.

Scenario: a layer-2 author follows the citation and passes `[ctx.locale]`. A request naming a locale the producer has no text for then skips rung 2 and lands on `en`, against `:105-106`. The PR body warns of this in acceptance note 7; the contract does not.

Fix: say in the section that a producer needs the request locale and the workspace default as two values, and that `ExecutionContext.locale` alone is the fold of both.

**S3 · should-fix · the View All arm of the field-mask sentence says more than the rule found.**

This is `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.user-text.ts:229-233` and its ten translations, fed by `packages/lint/src/validate-security-posture.ts:1435`. The rule reports only the bits that are inert (`:1418`). Under View All that is `readable: false` alone, and the edit lock still binds (`:1393-1396`). The param bag carries `bypass` but not which bits are inert. So the sentence says the restriction on the field "has no effect" and that View All "overrides field restrictions for all its holders".

Scenario, the PR's own fixture (`finding-user-text.test.ts:158-167`): `sys_user.email` with `readable: false, editable: false` under `viewAllRecords`. Holders can read the field and still cannot edit it. The sentence tells the admin the entry does nothing and offers "delete the field restriction", which would drop a lock that is in force. The developer `message` is exact on this point.

Fix: carry the inert half in `userTextParams` (read mask, edit lock, or both), and word the View All arm as a hidden field that is not hidden.

**Nits.** None affects the contract. Each may ride the patch round, since the head moves anyway, or stand as an accepted deviation.

- N1 · `index.ts:1218-1226` puts `FINDING_USER_TEXT_CATALOG`, `mergeUserTextCatalogs`, `renderUserText`, `userTextLocaleOf` and `SECURITY_POSTURE_USER_TEXT` on the root entry. The design names one caller, `findingUserMessage` through `./runtime`. Each extra name is public API of a fixed-group package.
- N2 · `validate-security-posture.user-text.ts:330-333` prescribes adding a check condition without the side effect the rule's `hint` exists to state (`validate-security-posture.ts:709-711`): a creator who is not the owner loses update unless a check admits them. The sentence is not false. It fits the native-read follow-up of open question 3.
- N3 · a sentence carries the rule's stand-in when the document has no name, such as `(permission set 0)` or a book index (`validate-security-posture.ts:1551`), which leaves an English fragment inside a localized sentence. The sentences also name API names (`crm_deal`, `owner_id`), where the envelope's platform producer keeps machine names out of `userMessage` (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/packaged-permission-set-lock.ts:277-279`). That is reasonable for a Studio author; one line in the catalog header would record the choice.

**Per file.**

- `contract.zod.ts`: does not hold as written (M1, S1, S2). What holds: the card's item 1 is stated on both envelopes, the fallback order is the one the card orders, "verbatim binds the consumer" agrees with the existing section, and every cited symbol exists where cited.
- `errors.zod.ts`: a faithful pointer to that section. It inherits M1 at `:415-416` and S1 in its `.describe()`.
- `protocol.zod.ts`: the key holds against the ruling and its first consumer. `rule` is untouched, the key is optional, absence means the consumer renders `message`, and `toIssue` can fill it in layer 2 with no further schema change. It inherits M1 only through the reference at `:1012-1014`.
- `finding-user-text.ts`: agrees with the contract sentence by sentence, which is why it carries M1. The rest agrees: the entry type requires `en`, a rule id has one catalog owner, and a finding with no params or no entry yields no sentence.
- `validate-security-posture.ts`: all eight push sites of the seven advisory ids set params, and the names agree with the catalog's table. The `remedy` split follows the `hint` split, and the opt-in is never prescribed where the runtime does not honour it. S3 at `:1435`.
- `validate-security-posture.user-text.ts`: seven ids in eleven locales, keyed by the rule's own id constants. S3, N2, N3. The English and Chinese sentences were read against each rule's `message` and `hint`; the other nine languages were not verified.
- `authoring-rules.ts`, `index.ts`, `runtime.ts`: the type and the exports agree with the contract. N1.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-tpz7ec`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV21cDQa3kVuDvC5s2`

**VERDICT: FAIL**
